title: Keyboard Manager isn’t saving the shortcut enable/disable toggle.
author: DerDemystifier
summary: Keyboard Manager shortcut enable states can fail to persist because the editor attempts to toggle a mapping ID absent from its in-memory dictionary; users also report backup omitting disabled shortcuts.
next_action: Reproduce against current stable using a migrated editorSettings.json and verify ID/state consistency across save, reopen, and backup.

confidence.rationale: The exception identifies a concrete failing state and several users confirm the persistence symptom.

judgment.rationale: The issue includes a precise UI sequence, screenshots, a concrete KeyNotFound error, multiple confirmations, and workarounds that point to editor state desynchronization.
evidence: The log records `ToggleSwitch_Toggled` failing because a mapping GUID was not present in the dictionary.
Multiple users report shortcuts becoming disabled again after closing and reopening the editor.
Deleting and recreating mappings sometimes clears the logged error, while backup reportedly restores only enabled mappings.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce against current stable using a migrated editorSettings.json and verify ID/state consistency across save, reopen, and backup.

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue is ready for maintainer reproduction, but the lightweight pass does not establish which migration, load, or save path owns the stale mapping ID.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager shortcut enable states can fail to persist because the editor attempts to toggle a mapping ID absent from its in-memory dictionary; users also report backup omitting disabled shortcuts.
known_information: The original report is against 0.99.1 and the discussion includes 0.100.2.
The issue affects shortcut enable-state persistence in the new editor.
A diagnostic log and screenshots are present in the report.
inferences: Migration or load-time normalization may leave displayed mappings whose IDs are absent from the dictionary used by the toggle handler.
issue_context.analysis: A controlled migrated-settings repro can distinguish serialization loss from an editor-only dictionary synchronization failure without asking reporters for data already supplied.
initial_investigation: Read the full report, all six comments, screenshots described in the body, and the supplied exception text.
Separated this persistence failure from the runtime shortcut failure tracked in #47812.

actions.label: Reproduce shortcut toggle persistence
actions.note: Maintainer-side verification only; this artifact performs no upstream write.

reproduce.title: Exercise migrated shortcut IDs across save and backup
prerequisites: A copy of pre-0.99 Keyboard Manager settings or a fixture with multiple enabled and disabled shortcuts
setup: Open the new Keyboard Manager editor and identify each mapping ID in editorSettings.json.
steps: Toggle one shortcut off and one on, save, close the editor, and reopen it.
Confirm each row retains its state and inspect the editor log for a missing mapping GUID.
Restart PowerToys and repeat the state check.
Create and restore a PowerToys backup and verify both enabled and disabled mappings remain present without duplicate IDs.
reproduce.expected_result: Every mapping keeps its enabled state through reopen, restart, and backup/restore; no toggle references an ID absent from the loaded dictionary.
